rejected_rule.statement: The setting aside of a deed of transfer in consequence of a decree entered in a Paulian action does not revest the property, which was the subject of the transfer, in the transferor. The fraudulent deed is only declared void so far as it is necessary to make the property available for execution.
rejected_rule.supporting_quote: "A fraudulent deed is not annulled but is only declared void so far as it is necessary to make the property available for execution." - Gunawardene v. Bilindahamy [1 C. W. R. 95.]
